stem: Smita knows that $(5, 12, 13)$ is a Baudhāyana triple. She multiplies every entry by $3$ to get $(15, 36, 39)$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Because $5^{2}+12^{2}=13^{2}$, multiplying by $3$ gives $(3\cdot 5)^{2}+(3\cdot 12)^{2}=(3\cdot 13)^{2}$, so $(15,36,39)$ is also a Baudhāyana triple.

teacher.key_rationale: Scaling every entry of a Baudhāyana triple by the same positive integer k preserves a²+b²=c². Here k=3, and 15²+36²=225+1296=1521=39². Option C confuses the side-sum with the squared relation.
